newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to meet Hong Kong's Martin Lee on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to meet Hong Kong's Martin Lee on Friday.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will meet with Martin Lee, a leader of Hong Kong's democracy movement, on Friday, White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said on Wednesday.
McCurry said Lee was scheduled to meet Vice President Al Gore at the White House on Friday, adding that Clinton would drop by the session.

Lee is on a lobbying mission in the United States ahead of the switch of Hong Kong from British rule to Chinese control on July 1, amid concern over indications that China wants to tighten controls on its political and civil liberties.

"The vice president will have a meeting with prominent Hong Kong parliamentarian Martin Lee on Friday ... and the president is expected to join that meeting in progress," McCurry told reporters at his regular midday briefing.
He added that he expected the meeting to take place on Friday afternoon, but said the exact time was not set.
In structuring Clinton's encounter with Lee as a "drop-by" visit during Gore's meeting, the White House appears at pains not to antagonize China over the session.

Washington is extremely sensitive about relations with China, particularly since an unofficial visit to the United States by Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui in 1995 caused a chill between Washington and Beijing that took months to thaw.
When Gore himself went to China last month, he did not visit Hong Kong, based on the advice of the State Department and National Security Council staff.
